caseno:
Criminal Revision No. 268 of 1986 (Comilla)
Criminal Revision No. 55(C)/88.
lawyer:
Syed Mahmud Hossain, Advocate -----For the Petitioner.
Mujibur Rahman, Advocate ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Syed Ahmed ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Abdul Khaleque and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
AK Badrul Huq, J.: The subject matter of challenge in this Rule issued on an application under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure at the instance of the informant-petitioner is the judgment and order of acquittal passed upon the accused-opposite-parties in a Session Case of the charge of murder and abetment under sections 302 and 109 of the Penal Code. 

 2. The accused-opposite parties being charged under sections 302 and 109 of the Penal Code faced trial before the First Court, Additional Sessions Judge, Comilla in Session Case No.142 of 1984 who acquitted them of the charge of the above sections. 

 5. Before adverting to the contentions pressed into service the background of the case may be summed up which are as follows: Dud Mia Mazumder, the father of the informant-petitioner is the deceased in the case whose dead body was recovered by the police of Chauddagram Police Station from the bed of Dakatia river at Hossainpur. The accused opposite party No.1, Abdul Khaleque is the son of the deceased Dud Mia Majumder and the full brother of the informant. The accused-opposite party Nos.2-5, Abul Kashem, Ali Ashraf, Azad Mia and Jharu Miah are Bhaira, cousin brother-in-law, full brother-in-law and father-in-law respectively of the accused opposite party No.1 Abdul Khaleque. The informant-petitioner lodged First Information Report with Chauddagram Police Station alleging inter alia, that his father deceased Dud Mia Majumder went to visit the house of his Behai Abdul Mannanat Palpan on 19-3-84 but he did not return home. In the morning of 21-3-84 on getting information of the missing incident of his father from his younger brother Babul Ahmed, he and other relations started searching for his father. In the morning of 24-3-84 he got information that the police of Chauddagram recovered a male dead body from Dakatia river at Hossainpur who identified the said dead body to be his father. The deceased has land dispute with Mohan Mia and others and it was suspected that out of enmity they murdered his father. 

 8. The accused opposite parties pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried putting forward a defence that Zainal Abedin and Eshahque were the real culprits but the informant, his brother and mother compromised the case with them after realising a large amount of money. The accused- opposite party Abdul Khaleque did not come to the terms and raised objection to the said compromise and for the said reason he and his father-in-law along with other relations have been entangled in the case falsely. 

 28. The learned trial Judge found fault with the prosecution story taking the view that in the First Information Report there is no mention that accused Abdul Khaleque took his father from his house on 19-3-1984 and the First Information Report being the earliest report to the police there was necessity of mentioning this fact in it and the omission to mention the said fact went against the prosecution. First Information Report is not an encyclopaedia. It is not the beginning and ending of every case. It is only a complaint to set the law or order in motion. It is only an initiative to move the machinery and to investigate into a cognizable offence. It is only at the investigation stage that all the details can be gathered and filled up. The First Information report thus should not be treated as the last word of the prosecution in the matter. So to reject the story on the ground of non-mentioning the fact in the First Information Report is to show an inadequate appreciation of criminal investigation and weight to be attached to evidence in criminal case. The fact that in the First Information Report there is no mention that accused Abdul Khaleque took his father from his home on 19-3-1984 is no ground to disbelieve the prosecution witnesses or for disbelieving the testimony of PWs 1, 2 and 5. The trial Judge, thus, appears to have committed a patent illegality in holding that omission to mention the said fact of the accused Abdul Khaleque taking his father from his house went against the prosecution. 

 29. Coming now to another finding of the trial Judge that withholding of the brother of the informant went against the prosecution case. PW 1, the informant, is the son of the deceased. PW 2 is the daughter of the deceased and the full sister of the Informant PW 1. PW 5 is the wife of the deceased and mother of the informant PW 1. It was not at all necessary to examine all the brothers of the informant in support of the prosecution case. It is not a case where none of the sons and daughters had been examined. Law does not require particular number of witnesses to prove a case and conviction may be founded even on the testimony of a solitary witness provided his credibility is not shaken by any adverse circumstances appearing on the record against him and the court at the same time is convinced that he is a truthful witness. As a general rule, a court can act on the testimony of a single witness though uncorroborated and one credible witness outweighs the testimony of a number of other witnesses of indifferent character. The well-known maxim that "evidence has to be weighed and not counted" has been given statutory placement in section 134 of the Evidence Act which provides as under. 

 "134. No particular number of witnesses shall in any case be required for the proof of any act" 

 30. The object of Revisional Jurisdiction under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is to confer the High Court Division a kind of paternal or supervisory jurisdiction in order to correct miscarriage of justice. The revisional power of the High Court Division vested in it by section 439 does not create any right in the litigant but only conserves the power of the High Court Division to see that justice is done in accordance with the recognised rules of Criminal Jurisprudence and that subordinate courts do not exceed the jurisdiction or abuse their powers vested in them by the court. It is to be borne in mind that the High Court Division does not function as a court of revision for permitting the guilty person to escape the just reward of their misdoing on the ground of an unsubstantial technicality. The power of the High Court Division under section 439 of the Code is thus indeed a power which has to be exercised in aid of justice and there is no form of injustice that the long arms of the court cannot reach because for administering and dispensing real and substantial justice the courts alone exist and there is no species of injustice which the High Court Division cannot correct where its interference is called for. The Revisional Jurisdiction of the High Court Division is in reality not a mere power but also a duty. Whether or not the High Court Division will exercise its Revisional jurisdiction in a given case must depend upon the facts and circumstances of that case only. 

 "The principles which have been consistently followed by this Court for justifying interference with orders of acquittals passed by, the High Courts have been clearly laid down in the cases Lalu vs State PLD 1959 SC 258 =12 DLR(SC) 225 and Fateh Muhammad vs Bagoo and others 12 DLR SC 200. Thus to indicate that unless it is possible to demonstrate with certainty that none of the grounds upon which the learned Judges-have purported to acquit is at' all supportable, this court will be reluctant to interfere even though upon the evidence on the record and the facts and Circumstances of the case this court might Well have come to a different conclusion if it was trying the case." 

 "We would, however, like to add that with the change of time and circumstances attending the administration of criminal justice time has come and experience also demand that the High Court Division will have to be a little more scrutinizing even in a case of acquittal because in the ultimate analysis it is interest of public justice and/or prevention of miscarriage of justice which prompt the court of revision to interfere in a particular case. As to what should, therefore, the scope of inquiry be in revision against acquittal when findings of fact are assailed, it may be said that the court of revision can legitimately examine whether correct principles relating to appraisal of evidence has been followed or not, whether some material piece of evidence has been overlooked or misappreciated which could have a profound bearing on the order of acquittal and things like that. Misappreciation of evidence is not ordinarily a ground for interference with an order of acquittal but to say that misappreciation of evidence is never a sufficient ground for interference with an acquittal, says Corrnelius CJ in the case of Abdur Rashid Khondker vs Chandu Master & ors 16 DLR (SC) 605 is to ignore the existence of degree of misappreciation, from the very grossest form, exhibiting perversity, to the mere ignoring of certain side aspects arising out of a piece of evidence. We respectfully agree with the learned Chief Justice when he says that "for the correct exercise of the revisionary power in such cases, and particularly where the revision is brought against an original order of acquittal, the High Court should in order to ensure that justice is seen to be done, survey the case, in its factual and evidentary aspects and should find where misappreciation of evidence is alleged, what the misappreciation consists in and what is its degree and finally, whether it has had a determinative effect upon the final conclusion". 

 33. On reading of the judgment under challenge it appears that the trial Judge failed to apply his mind judicially to the evidences, materials and legal aspects of the case. The trial Judge failed to discuss the evidences of all the prosecution witnesses including the vital evidence of PW 5 who is no other than the wife of the deceased and mother of both the informant-petitioner and accused- opposite party Abdul Khaleque. The impugned judgment contains speculative arguments and lacks the judicial balancing of facts. The judgment, thus, suffers from a manifest error resulting in a gross miscarriage of justice. The interest of public justice, therefore, requires interference for the correction of the manifest illegality and also for the prevention of flagrant miscarriage of justice and the setting aside of the impugned order of acquittal is demanded. 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment is set aside and the case is sent back to the learned Judge for fresh disposal in accordance with law. The learned trial Judge will secure the attendance of the accused-opposite parties. Since the case is of the year of 1984, the learned trial Judge is directed to dispose of the same within 4(four) months of the receipt of the copy of the judgment as well as record of the case. The expression of opinion on the present evidence with respect to the commission of the alleged offence would not be binding upon the trial Judge and in disposing of the case, he may not be, also, influenced by any observation made by us and he will unhesitatingly reach his own conclusion on the evidences and materials on record.
